sph_interpretive_translation: One who sustains damage to wealth, grain, or property for a period of four years shall regain full ownership and authority over it by divine right.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is restored through continuity of claim and conscious reclamation
Causation aligns with uninterrupted intent and capacity to reclaim
Capacity-based responsibility is measured in sustained engagement over time
Restoration logic operates through sequential completion and energetic alignment
Consciousness alignment determines rightful ownership beyond temporal loss
executable_legal_axioms: IF an individual demonstrates sustained intent and action toward reclaiming lost property for four years, THEN automatic restoration of ownership rights SHALL occur
IF no external opposition arises during the four-year claim period, THEN the claimant's title SHALL be self-validating
IF material evidence supports continuous assertion of ownership, THEN legal systems SHALL recognize the restoration as complete without punitive process
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that prolonged, unopposed assertion of ownership constitutes prima facie evidence of lawful restoration. The threshold of responsibility lies in sustained capacity to reclaim, not in punitive validation.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through continuous claim and absence of disruption. Anupūrvaśaḥ reflects the sequential unfolding of ownership reassertion. Responsibility is proportional to demonstrated capacity. The non-punitive reality rule confirms that ownership renews naturally when consciousness is aligned with intent.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Four-year continuous assertion validates self-restoration
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Claimant assumes full energetic and legal ownership upon completion
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Legal system recognizes the inherent capacity of the individual to reclaim authority
Integrity Reintegration Sequence: Ownership is restored without adversarial judgment or punitive measures
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands executed. Ownership renews through conscious continuity. Dharma is restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
